title: Appear2Meaning: A Cross-Cultural Benchmark for Structured Cultural Metadata Inference from Images
abstract: arXiv:2604.07338v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Museum records express how people understand heritage objects through cultural and historical relations. Recovering these human attributions from images is a technical challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We introduce Appear2Meaning, a cross-cultural benchmark of 750 museum objects for image-only recovery of title, culture, period, origin, and creator. Its evaluation framework distinguishes field-level from complete-record compatibility and uses human validation for semantic judgement. Across nine VLMs, mean field accuracy is 36.16--49.82%; 7.20--17.02% of records have all four contextual fields compatible, and 2.13--7.87% have all five, including title. For the two tested models, image-only input yields 12.6--32.2 percentage points higher reference compatibility for culture, period, and origin than a museum-and-title-only control.

translated_title: Appear2Meaning：一个用于从图像推断结构化文化元数据的跨文化基准
translated_abstract: 博物馆记录通过文化和历史关系表达了人们如何理解遗产物品。从图像中恢复这些人工赋予的归属信息，对视觉语言模型（VLM）来说是一项技术挑战。我们提出了Appear2Meaning，这是一个包含750件博物馆物品的跨文化基准数据集，用于仅凭图像恢复标题、文化、时期、产地和创作者五类信息。其评估框架区分了字段级别的兼容性与完整记录的兼容性，并采用人工验证进行语义判断。在九个VLM模型上，平均字段准确率为36.16%–49.82%；7.20%–17.02%的记录在所有四个上下文字段上均兼容，而包含标题在内的全部五个字段均兼容的记录仅占2.13%–7.87%。对于测试的两个模型，仅图像输入在文化、时期和产地方面的参考兼容性比仅使用博物馆名称和标题的对照组高出12.6–32.2个百分点。
tldr: 提出了包含750件博物馆物品的跨文化基准Appear2Meaning，用于评估视觉语言模型仅凭图像推断标题、文化、时期、产地和创作者等结构化文化元数据的能力，结果显示当前模型的完整记录兼容率仍然很低。
en_tdlr: Introduces Appear2Meaning, a cross-cultural benchmark of 750 museum objects for evaluating vision-language models' image-only inference of structured cultural metadata (title, culture, period, origin, creator), revealing that complete-record compatibility remains low across nine state-of-the-art VLMs.
